answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can require each agent to stake a small deposit before its first voyage through the marketplace, with the stake returned only after peers attest its work. Honest agents build a verifiable signal of reliability from completed jobs, while a fake identity that behaves badly loses its stake and must pay again to re-enter. A signed ledger entry acts like a quill's mark, tying reputation to one identity so creating many fake agents costs real money each time.
